senses.gloss: general rule, principle. Sifra K’dosh., Par. 2, ch. IV (ref. to Lev. XIX, 18) זה כ׳ גדול וכ׳ this (‘love thy neighbor as thyself’) is the most important principle in the Law.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 7:1">Sabb. VII, 1</cite>.
Ḥull. III, 1 זה הכ׳ this is the general rule; a. v. fr.—Trnsf. בִּכְלַל, לִכְלַל under the influence of.

<cite ref="Sifrei Bamidbar 157:9">Sifré Num. 157</cite> <he>לפי שהיה בכ׳ כעס בא לכ׳ טעות</he> because he was under the influence of anger, he came under the influence of mistaken judgment; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 786:14">Yalk. ib. 786</cite>; a. fr.

<cite ref="Berakhot 49b:16">Ber. 49ᵇ</cite> <he>לעולם אל … מן הכ׳</he> a person must never exclude himself from the community (by saying, ‘Praise ye’, instead of ‘Let us praise’). Mekh. Bo., Pisḥa, s. 18 <he>ולפי שהוציא … מן הכ׳ וכ׳</he> and as he excluded himself from the community (by saying ‘you’) &c.; a. e.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 123a:21">B. Bath. 123ᵃ</cite> <he>בכְלָלָן אתה וכ׳</he> as their sum total you find seventy (<cite ref="Genesis 46:27">Gen. XLVI, 27</cite>), whereas the detailed record counts only sixty nine.

senses.gloss: generalization, statement by implication, opp. פרט specification; inclusion, comprehension under a class.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 26b:10">Ber. 26ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>עד ועד בכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="P00111"><he>עַד</he></cite>.—Sifra introd. <he>מכ׳ ופרט מפרט וּכְ׳ וכ׳</he> interpretation based upon a general law followed by specification, or specification followed by generalization.
<cite ref="Berakhot 26b:10">Ib.</cite> <he>כל דבר שהיה בכ׳ וכ׳</he> when a law is once laid down in general, and in another place a specification is given (e.g.
<cite ref="Leviticus 7:37">Lev. VII, 37</cite>, a.
<cite ref="Leviticus 7:20">ib. 20</cite>), it is stated specifically not for its own sake alone, but as applicable to the whole class.

<cite ref="Leviticus 7:20">Ib.</cite> beg. <he>מכ׳ ופרט וּכְ׳ אי אתה דן וכ׳</he> if a general rule is followed by a specification and this again by a generalization, you must be guided by the specification (e.g.
<cite ref="Deuteronomy 14:26">Deut. XIV, 26</cite>).

Tosef. Sot. VIII, 10; Sot. 37ᵃ ברוך בכ׳ … ארור בכ׳ וכ׳ ‘blessed be’ was pronounced on Mount Gerizim in general (corresp. to the general curse, Deut. XXVII, 26) and was specified (corresp. to ib. 15—25) ; ‘cursed be’ was pronounced on Mount Ebal in general (ib. 26) &c.; a. fr.—מִכְּ׳ by implication.
Ned. 11ᵃ, a. fr. מכ׳ לאו אתה שומע הן from no you understand yes, v. הֵן.—
<cite ref="Pesachim 16b:9">Pes. 16ᵇ</cite> <he>שהותרה מִכְּלָלָהּ וכ׳</he> which was permitted (dispensed with), by implication, for a community (if unclean, derived fr.
<cite ref="Numbers 9:2">Num. IX, 2</cite>, v.
<cite ref="Pesachim 77a">Pes. 77ᵃ</cite>).
Ḥull. 37ᵇ מכ׳ דטרפה וכ׳ this proves by implication that t’refah is not the same as &c.; a. v. fr.—לאו … כ׳ not at all (cmp. כְּלוּם).
Ib. 20ᵇ; a. fr.—[Mekh. Bo, beg. כ׳ לדברות, read: כֶּלִי.]—Pl. כְּלָלוֹת (fem.).
<cite ref="Nazir 48b:3">Naz. 48ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Sotah 37b:1">Sot. 37ᵇ</cite>.

<cite ref="Eruvin 27a:2">Erub. 27ᵃ</cite> <he>אין למדין מן הכ׳ וכ׳</he> from general rules (the use of the word <he>כל</he>, as <cite ref="Mishnah Eruvin 3:1">ib. III, 1</cite>) we must not derive anything, not even when an exception is stated (as there may be other exceptions); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 32">Ex. R. s. 32</cite>, beg. <he>כְּלָלִים</he>.
